entities.name: Grepper
entities.how_described: 本集嘉宾 Jad Naous 创办的 10 人公司：把客户日志流过滤提纯信号、降低约 90% 的遥测/可观测性成本，再把这些信号喂给 AI 层去做故障排查与可靠性运维。

entities.name: 智能体 (agent)
entities.how_described: 本集把智能体说成编程工作流的核心：子智能体通过命令行保持持久会话、互相提问审查 PR；在运维侧，智能体不负责预测，而是在收到『有东西变了』的信号后跑假设、查代码、做实验、逐步收窄问题。

evidence.quote: Like the first thing that I do is I ask that agent to do it, ask the tech leads to review the PR doc.

evidence.quote: Because the goal is not actually having the agent try to predict, but have it get a signal that something changed deterministically.

entities.name: 可观测性 (observability)
entities.how_described: 本集说企业把 5%-20% 的基础设施开支花在可观测性上，实际上是购买『可靠性』的代理，但随微服务架构数据量膨胀，其边际可靠性收益正在趋平——这是 Grepr 切入的问题。

evidence.quote: Everybody would say, first it was infrastructure and then observability.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: First, people were spending somewhere between 5% and 20% of what they spend on infrastructure, on observability.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: And so they were putting money into observability as a proxy for reliability.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: There was much deeper market penetration for observability and kind of the volume of data that you're collecting and the cost of observability was actually starting to grow faster than the units of function that you're outputting.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: And the marginal rate or like the marginal increase in reliability for every additional dollar you're spending on observability was just flattening out.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: And so the question was, can we actually solve that problem and bring back that increase in reliability, that marginal increase in reliability, not necessarily by spending more money on observability, but some other way.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

evidence.quote: And so the thinking was like, okay, great, if we can figure out what is the signal, what is the noise, can we actually turn the observability data that you're collecting that's mostly fluff and mostly insurance at this point and do that kind of extraction of information upstream, do whatever you need upstream and be able to ultimately massively reduce the cost of observability downstream.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02

entities.name: 分布式系统 (distributed systems)
entities.how_described: 本集说 Jad 的团队做的就是分布式系统与分布式算法这类硬核生意，AI 无法替人处理其中的复杂度；Martin 补充运行分布式集群的『肮脏秘密』长期就是靠人来管理。

evidence.quote: In my experience for the things that we do, that is the case because we build distributed systems and distributed algorithms and like your brain has to handle the complexity because like AI doesn't do it.

entities.name: 根因排查 (root cause)
entities.how_described: 本集说常见 AI SRE 方案从滞后指标出发回溯根因、所以不管用；Grepr 反过来先在全部日志里大规模聚类找出没见过的新模式，再让 AI 一步步收窄问题。

evidence.quote: It's you know that's why those don't work because like backtracking into a root cause is actually very problematic and so instead what we're doing is doing it the other way around which is can we actually start by figuring out if there's something different in your environment that has changed like can we do a large-scale clustering a large-scale kind of figure out a needle in a haystack something that is different and now so you're assuming that it was working
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_02
